title: Almost Palindrome Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of integers, return `true` if the list can become a palindrome after deleting **at most one** node from anywhere in the list, and `false` otherwise.

Aim for `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Split the list into `left` (first `ceil(n / 2)` nodes) and `right` (last `floor(n / 2)` nodes) using fast/slow pointers, noting whether `n` is odd (`fast.next == null`), then reverse `right` in-place.

Walk `p1` (in `left`) and `p2` (in reversed `right`) until the first mismatch: deleting `p1` succeeds if remaining `p1.next` matches `p2` element-for-element; deleting `p2` succeeds if remaining `p2.next` matches `p1` and, when `n` is odd, the two leftover nodes at the end of `left` are equal.

examples.explanation: [1, 2, 3, 2, 1] is already a palindrome (zero deletions needed).
No single deletion can make [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] a palindrome.
